# local 0007: mcs51: reads such as *a[1][1] through an element of a nested array of pointers in data memory first store the pointer through itself

- Category: [Trivial fixes](../../fix-trivial.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. ds390, whose register allocator also calls ptrPseudoSymConvert, was not built.
- Patch: [local-0007.patch](../../patches/local-0007.patch), commit [`94ad6cb0f`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/94ad6cb0f04bd8c9e4da4843bd6da5f12af5859b). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.

```diff
diff --git a/src/SDCCptropt.c b/src/SDCCptropt.c
index 7ddaa48c7..df4efc0ef 100644
--- a/src/SDCCptropt.c
+++ b/src/SDCCptropt.c
@@ -414,6 +414,8 @@ ptrPseudoSymConvert (symbol * sym, iCode * dic, const char *name)
   /* now this really is an assignment to itself, make it so;
      it will be optimized out later */
   dic->op = '=';
+  /* an assignment whose result is marked as an address is a pointer set */
+  SET_ISADDR (IC_RESULT (dic), 0);
   ReplaceOpWithCheaperOp (&IC_RIGHT (dic), IC_RESULT (dic));
   IC_LEFT (dic) = NULL;
 #endif
```
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For `rdl` and `rdc` below, the compiler emits a store of the pointer through itself in front of
the read. The file was compiled on r17176 with `sdcc -mmcs51 p2.c` and run in ucsim.

```c
long v = 0x11223344;
char buf[3] = { 0x55, 0x66, 0x77 };
long *a[2][2];
struct s { char c; char *names[2]; } st;

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[9];

long rdl (void) { return *a[1][1]; }
char rdc (void) { return *st.names[1]; }

void main (void)
{
  unsigned char i;

  a[1][1] = &v;
  st.names[1] = buf;
  res[0] = (rdl () == 0x11223344);
  res[1] = rdc ();
  for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
    res[2 + i] = ((unsigned char *)&v)[i];
  for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)
    res[6 + i] = buf[i];
  for (;;);
}
```

After the run `res` holds `00 0c 08 00 40 11 0c 00 40`, and `01 55 44 33 22 11 55 66 77` is
expected. `v` is at address 0x08 and `buf` at 0x0c, so the three bytes of each generic pointer
have replaced the first three bytes of the object that it points to. `rdl` loads the pointer into
`dptr` and `b`, calls `__gptrput` three times with the bytes of the pointer, and then reads with
`__gptrget`.

With `--stack-auto` the result is this one too. With `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, and
`--model-large --stack-auto` it is the expected one, because the arrays are not in data memory.
For arrays that are declared `__data`, the fault occurs with these models as well.

In the assembly for the small model, the store is also present for `*a[0][0]`, for a
three-dimensional array, and for `*sa[1].names[1]`. For elements of the type `__data long *` it is
`mov @r0,(_ad + 0x0003)`. It is absent for the one-dimensional array `long *a1[4]`, for `*a[1][i]`
with a variable index, for elements of the type `__xdata long *`, and for the write
`*a[1][1] = 5`.

## Cause

For unary `*`, `ast2iCode` in `src/SDCCicode.c` calls
`geniCodeDerefPtr (geniCodeRValue (left, false), lvl)`. When the pointer is an element of an array
that is itself an array element or a struct member, `geniCodeRValue` emits the
`GET_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` that reads the pointer and returns the result operand of that iCode itself.
`geniCodeDerefPtr` sets `isaddr` on the operand that it is given, so the flag is set in the iCode.
For other pointer operands `geniCodeRValue` returns a copy.

In `src/mcs51/ralloc.c`, iTemps whose only definition is a read through a near pointer that can
be rematerialized become pseudo symbols at that address. `ptrPseudoSymConvert` in
`src/SDCCptropt.c` changes the read to the assignment `iTemp = iTemp` and leaves `isaddr` set on
the result. The macro `POINTER_SET` holds for such an assignment, and the code generator emits a
store through the pointer. After register allocation, the iCode for `*a[1][1]` has
`*(iTemp3) := iTemp3`.

## Fix

`ptrPseudoSymConvert` clears `isaddr` on the result with `SET_ISADDR` when it changes the read to
an assignment. The macro replaces the operand with a copy, so the pointer operand of the read
that follows keeps the flag. `cseBBlock` in `src/SDCCcse.c` clears the flag in this way where it
changes a pointer read to an assignment.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/deref-ptr-array-elem.c` reads `*a[1][1]`, `*a[0][0]`, `*st.names[1]`,
and `*np[1][0]`, where `np` has one-byte pointers. The arrays and the struct are `__data`. On
r17192 with the earlier patches of the series, 10 of its 14 assertions fail on each of
mcs51-small, mcs51-medium, mcs51-large, mcs51-small-stack-auto, and mcs51-large-stack-auto. With
the patch the test passes on these five, on mcs51-huge, on host, on stm8, and on ucz80.

For mcs51-small, every other regression test has the code size and the tick count that it has
without the patch. Apart from comments, the assembly of the 1083 files of the mcs51 libraries is
unchanged. With the patch series of this report up to the patch for local 0001 applied to r17192,
the regression suite ran without a failure for the nine targets above. The diagnostics suite ran
without a failure for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

`src/ds390/ralloc.c` calls `ptrPseudoSymConvert` for such iTemps too. ds390 was not built.

## Related

Bug #2691 concerns the address of such elements, `&a[i][j]`. Its patch does not change this
defect, which was found with its test cases.
